heading: FYLO documents and queue, in every Yon language
body:
Configure the `fylo` driver and every Yon language except Lua can use the FYLO document store and its queue through the injected DataSource. Lua has no tab here, because the build refuses a DataSource in Lua Yon code with `TY2015` (ADR 0085): write the class that needs it in another Yon language. Choose one language and copy server/application.json with that language's service and controller (Go also needs its three models). GET /events answers {"found":"deploy","patched":7,"pages":2,"seen":3,"job":{"app":"web"},"gone":true,"dropped":true}.

Collections: `createCollection(name)` creates a collection and does nothing when it already exists, `dropCollection(name)` answers false when there was nothing to drop, and `collectionExists(name)` answers true or false. A collection name has 2 to 64 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starts and ends with a letter or digit, and is not a FYLO reserved word, so `hd-events` works and `../etc`, `hd_events` and `Events` are refused with `TY2160`. Store tables on FYLO follow the same rule.

Documents: `insert(collection, document)` stores a document and answers it with the `id` that FYLO assigned (Go answers the id itself). FYLO assigns identifiers, so a document that already has an id is refused. `findById(collection, id)` answers the newest version of the document, or null when there is none, like `findById` in Spring Data. `patch(collection, id, fields)` changes only the named top-level fields and keeps every other field, like `Update.set` in Spring Data MongoDB: a null value stores null, and a nested object replaces the old one. The change and the read of the result happen in one step, so patches that run at the same time never lose each other's fields. It answers the patched document, or null when the id does not exist, and it cannot change the id. `deleteById(collection, id)` answers true, or false when the document was already gone.

Scrolling: `scroll(collection, where, cursor, size)` reads one page of at most `size` documents (1 to 100, 20 by default) in id order, which is the order FYLO created them in. `where` is null or an object of field values that must all be equal. Pass a null cursor (an empty string in Go and Rust) for the first page, and then the `nextCursor` of the page before; `nextCursor` is null on the last page. There is no offset and no 10,000 limit, like the scroll API (`Window`) of Spring Data. The first page takes a snapshot of every match, so later inserts and changes do not move documents between pages; it may take up to 30 seconds, and the matches of one scroll must fit in 8 MiB. A cursor is opaque text that lasts 15 minutes in the server that made it; reading the same cursor again reads the same page. A server keeps at most 8 scrolls open: a ninth scroll ends the oldest one, and its cursor then counts as expired. After a cursor expires or the server restarts, start again from the first page.

Queue: FYLO has a durable queue, and DataSource reaches it with no broker. `publish(topic, payload, key)` adds a message and answers its id; publishing again with the same key and payload answers the first id instead of adding a copy. `claim(topic, group, maxMessages, leaseMs)` hands out up to `maxMessages` deliveries (1 to 100), each with `id`, `receipt`, `attempt` and `payload`, and hides them from other workers of the same group for `leaseMs` milliseconds. `ack(topic, group, delivery)` finishes a delivery; `nack(topic, group, delivery, delayMs)` gives it back to be claimed again after `delayMs`. A delivery that is not acknowledged before its lease ends is claimed again, so delivery is at least once: write handlers that can safely run twice. After the third attempt FYLO keeps the message as a dead letter. A receipt from an expired lease is refused. Topic and group names have 1 to 127 ASCII letters, digits, dots, hyphens and underscores.

These methods need the FYLO datasource; the SQL drivers refuse them with `TY2160`. In Go, `FindById` and `Patch` decode into a model and answer whether the document exists, `Scroll` answers a `DocumentWindow`, and `Claim` answers `QueueDelivery` values; `Decode` turns their JSON into your models.

C++ has no tab here, because C++ Yon code has only route controllers so far: the build refuses `Service` in C++ with `TY1308` (ADR 0099).
